forces.title: Soaring demand for critical minerals drives global mining growth
forces.description: Global demand for critical minerals like lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese, and rare earth elements (REEs) is projected to grow significantly through 2040. These minerals are crucial for electrification, renewable energy, battery storage, digital infrastructure, AI, and defense supply chains, positioning mining as a vital industry for the global economy and driving unprecedented growth in production capacity.
forces.source_title: Harnessing AI to make mining safer

forces.title: Mining's inherent hazards and stalled fatality reduction pose persistent risks
forces.description: Despite technological improvements, mining remains one of the most hazardous industries globally, with fatality rates exceeding transportation, construction, and manufacturing. Fatal injury rates have plateaued in recent years after decades of improvement. This persistent challenge leads to devastating human tolls, significant financial liabilities, production shutdowns, and long-term reputational damage for mining companies.
forces.source_title: Harnessing AI to make mining safer

forces.title: Rapid critical mineral expansion creates capability and contractor gaps
forces.description: The global push to scale critical mineral production has introduced significant capability and contractor management gaps, particularly in emerging markets. Rapid workforce growth and increased reliance on contractors lead to variability in safety standards, inconsistent training, inadequate fatigue management, and limited frontline oversight, posing substantial operational and safety risks for mining companies.
forces.source_title: Harnessing AI to make mining safer

forces.title: AI tools significantly enhance mining productivity and safety operations
forces.description: The adoption of agentic AI tools offers significant opportunities to improve safety and productivity in mining. AI-enabled video analytics can monitor CCTV feeds for deviations, identify hazards, and generate incident reports. AI and digital tools also strengthen contractor safety management. These applications improve operational discipline, reduce disruptions, and foster proactive safety cultures, making mines safer, more efficient, and sustainable.
forces.source_title: Harnessing AI to make mining safer

forces.title: Softer global metal prices depress revenues for Irish metals sector
forces.description: The Irish metals sector faces headwinds from softer global metal prices heading into 2025/26. This trend necessitates careful purchasing decisions and strong inventory discipline to mitigate financial exposure, as reduced pricing power can erode margins. While the sector shows resilience, declining prices pose a challenge to revenue stability and overall profitability.

forces.title: Rising raw material and labor costs pressure Irish metals margins
forces.description: The Irish metals sector is experiencing persistent raw material and labor cost pressures. These elevated input costs make it challenging for firms to maintain profitability, especially if global base-metal prices soften. Businesses must review procurement strategies and pricing arrangements to assess how much cost inflation can be passed on to customers without weakening relationships.

forces.title: Geopolitical uncertainty and tariffs impact Irish metals trade policies
forces.description: Uncertainty surrounding international trade policies and tariffs, exacerbated by geopolitical tensions, poses a key risk to the Irish metals sector. This environment can affect competitiveness in export markets and disrupt global supply chains. Firms need to monitor tariff exposure and strategic decisions by major multinational players to navigate potential market volatility and maintain strong liquidity.

forces.title: Africa's rich critical mineral endowment boosts global supply
forces.description: Africa holds over a quarter of the world's known critical mineral reserves, including high-grade deposits of lithium, cobalt, manganese, graphite, REEs, tungsten, and vanadium. This exceptional endowment, coupled with rising global demand for energy transition and technology minerals, positions Africa as a central player in the emerging minerals economy, positively impacting global and European supply chains for these vital resources.
forces.source_title: African bedrock: How the continent’s minerals can help power the world

forces.title: Supply constraints for critical minerals hinder global availability
forces.description: The supply of several critical materials, including REEs, nickel, and manganese, faces persistent constraints globally due to challenges in ore quality, processing, and infrastructure. These limitations, combined with rising global demand, exacerbate supply tightness. Geopolitical conflicts and resource nationalism further disrupt mineral flows, impacting investor sentiment and the security of critical mineral supply chains for European markets.
forces.source_title: African bedrock: How the continent’s minerals can help power the world

forces.title: African mines face higher costs due to operational inefficiencies
forces.description: African mining operations are generally more costly than their global peers, even with similar ore quality. This is attributed to inherent inefficiencies in mining and processing, which erode the continent's geological advantage. These higher operating costs impact profitability and make African projects less competitive, affecting the overall cost structure of critical minerals sourced globally for Europe.
forces.source_title: African bedrock: How the continent’s minerals can help power the world

forces.title: G20 Critical Minerals Framework promotes mineral sovereignty and local value-addition
forces.description: The G20 Critical Minerals Framework (2025 Johannesburg Summit) reframes global minerals trade towards inclusive growth and sustainable development. It prioritizes securing supply chains against geopolitical risks and shifting developing nations from raw exports to local value-addition. This structural change influences investment strategies and supply chain resilience for critical minerals, impacting European procurement and trade dynamics.
forces.source_title: African bedrock: How the continent’s minerals can help power the world

forces.title: High-grade iron ore offers potential for reduced CO₂ emissions
forces.description: High-grade iron ore, such as the 65% iron content found in Guinea's Simandou project (the world's largest untapped reserve), presents an upside driver for decarbonization. This ore has the potential to reduce CO₂ emissions from ironmaking by 5% per metric ton compared to lower-grade ore, as it requires fewer coal-based inputs. This aligns with global decarbonization ambitions.
forces.source_title: African bedrock: How the continent’s minerals can help power the world

forces.title: African early-stage mine development lags due to various hurdles
forces.description: Early-stage mine development in Africa significantly lags other regions, with annual exploration spending being half of Australia's or Canada's. Projects are often stalled by high country risk, legal and jurisdictional uncertainty, permitting delays, community conflict, and financing hurdles. This underdevelopment in Africa limits the pipeline of new critical mineral projects available to global markets, including Europe.
forces.source_title: African bedrock: How the continent’s minerals can help power the world

forces.title: Infrastructure underinvestment constrains African mining project development
forces.description: Infrastructure underinvestment is a major constraint in African mining. Essential infrastructure like roads, rail, and power is often limited or unreliable, driving up project costs and risks. High power costs, grid instability, and constrained rail networks (often dating from the 19th/20th century) hinder development, especially for landlocked producers, limiting the efficient transport of minerals to global markets.
forces.source_title: African bedrock: How the continent’s minerals can help power the world

forces.title: Productivity gap and talent shortage challenge African mining efficiency
forces.description: Africa’s mining industry suffers from a productivity gap compared to other regions, partly due to lower technology adoption and digitalization. A shortage of skilled talent, combined with historical support for labor-intensive models, further compounds this challenge. While modernization and new projects offer improvement, these issues limit operational efficiency and increase overall costs for critical mineral production.
forces.source_title: African bedrock: How the continent’s minerals can help power the world

forces.title: Operational excellence and capital efficiency boost mining profitability
forces.description: Optimizing capital expenditures (up to 15% reduction) and operational expenditures (up to 20% reduction) through capital and operational excellence can significantly improve cost positions and increase cash flows in mining. Strategies include right-sizing starter projects, phasing development, prioritizing higher-grade ore, improving planning to shorten timelines by up to a year, and enhancing mineral recovery for a 5% revenue uplift.
forces.source_title: African bedrock: How the continent’s minerals can help power the world

forces.title: Innovative mining technologies accelerate development and reduce costs
forces.description: Adopting innovative mining technologies is the fastest lever for improving productivity. Technology innovation can increase throughput by 12-22% and reduce operational expenditures by 8-13%. Advanced geophysical methods and AI can refine drill targeting (15-30% hit rate increase), while AI-enabled rigs reduce drilling costs by 15-30%. Smart plants, autonomous equipment, and centralized operations centers boost overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) and recovery.
forces.source_title: African bedrock: How the continent’s minerals can help power the world

forces.title: Geopolitical issues profoundly impact critical minerals supply chains
forces.description: Geopolitical tensions and ongoing conflicts exert acute pressure on mission-critical sectors like critical minerals, significantly impacting trade and investment flows. This necessitates a strategic rather than reactive approach to geopolitics, as many firms currently lack systematic integration of geopolitical insights into core business decisions, leaving them unprepared for future disruptions in vital supply chains that affect Europe.
forces.source_title: From Crisis Reaction to Strategic Geopolitical Response

forces.title: Middle East conflict triggers high energy inflation for industrial raw materials
forces.description: The ongoing Middle East conflict is causing high energy inflation and widespread supply chain disruption, significantly impacting industrial raw materials. Specifically, it affects inputs for metal processing and fertilizers, such as sulfur (25% of global supply). Higher feedstock costs and supply chain volatility lead to increased operating expenses and raw material costs, creating a headwind for diversified mining operations.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: AI-driven safety is becoming a foundation of competitive advantage in mining
viewpoints.description: McKinsey states that intelligent safety, enabled by AI and automation, is becoming a core competitive advantage in mining. It's explicitly linked to productivity, ESG performance, and long-term resilience, contributing to safer, more productive, efficient, and sustainable mines. Companies adopting these solutions are expected to gain a significant edge in the sector.
viewpoints.source_title: Harnessing AI to make mining safer

viewpoints.title: Irish metals sector shows resilience despite global price and cost headwinds
viewpoints.description: Allianz Ireland indicates that the Irish metals sector, supported by construction, engineering, manufacturing, and agri-business, maintains generally stable trading conditions. Despite moderating global metal prices, persistent raw material and labor cost pressures, and trade policy uncertainties, the sector has demonstrated resilience, though it faces moderate risk heading into 2025/26.

viewpoints.title: Africa's mining sector at inflection point, must convert geological advantage into competitiveness
viewpoints.description: McKinsey believes Africa's mining sector is at a crucial juncture, holding critical minerals vital for global energy and technology transitions. However, realizing this potential requires overcoming significant challenges in infrastructure, skills, and governance. Strategic actions like developing clusters, enhancing operational excellence, and deploying smart technology are essential for a resilient and competitive future.
viewpoints.source_title: African bedrock: How the continent’s minerals can help power the world

viewpoints.title: Geopolitics essential for strategic planning in critical minerals and other sectors
viewpoints.description: BCG emphasizes that geopolitics is now a core business consideration, particularly for critical minerals, with 80% of companies reporting significant exposure. While capabilities are strengthening, only 15% systematically embed geopolitics into core decisions. BCG advocates for a shift from reactive crisis response to proactive strategic planning to inform forward-looking investment and innovation decisions.
viewpoints.source_title: From Crisis Reaction to Strategic Geopolitical Response

demand_drivers.description: Global demand for materials essential for energy transition, including critical minerals like lithium, cobalt, nickel, manganese, and rare earth elements, is projected to grow significantly.

market_sizing.methodology: McKinsey's Global Materials Perspective 2025 estimates demand for energy transition materials. While a specific value is not given, the growth rate indicates significant market expansion.
market_sizing.source_title: African bedrock: How the continent’s minerals can help power the world

demand_drivers.description: A 10% reduction in unit production costs, driven by structural interventions, is estimated to make more mines profitable, increasing total output by 25-30%.
Expanded revenues from upstream suppliers and additional value retained through local mineral processing contribute to the total economic value unlocked.

new_opportunities.description: Coordinated clustering approaches in Africa could fundamentally alter project economics by spreading infrastructure costs, reducing risk, and creating investible regional ecosystems.
Stronger capabilities in capital-project execution, operational excellence, and deployment of technology innovation (e.g., gen AI) can significantly improve mining efficiency and profitability.

market_sizing.methodology: McKinsey research on African mining. Calculated by combining increased production from a hypothesized 10% reduction in unit production costs (leading to a 25-30% output increase) with expanded revenues from upstream suppliers and additional value retained through local mineral processing.
market_sizing.source_title: African bedrock: How the continent’s minerals can help power the world

demand_drivers.description: The Simandou project is the world's largest untapped high-grade iron ore reserve, poised to meet global demand for high-quality iron ore, especially for lower-CO2 steel production.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected annual production capacity for the Simandou project in Guinea upon reaching full production.
market_sizing.source_title: African bedrock: How the continent’s minerals can help power the world

pnl_drivers.description: Less than 10% of this pipeline has secured financing or progressed to construction/feasibility stages, indicating significant hurdles to unlock this value.

market_sizing.methodology: Total pipeline value of critical mineral projects across Africa, based on MineSpans data, indicating the potential for future development.
market_sizing.source_title: African bedrock: How the continent’s minerals can help power the world

demand_drivers.description: Integrating investments and sharing infrastructure in geographically proximate mining operations can improve ore production volumes by up to 5% and reduce unit costs by about 20%.

new_opportunities.description: Clustering creates investible regional ecosystems, spreads risk, and secures better purchase agreements, making projects more attractive to investors and enabling in-country value addition.
Mining clusters can address environmental, social, and governance challenges systemically through shared decarbonization assets, coordinated biodiversity management, and pooled community resources.

market_sizing.methodology: Estimated revenue potential from critical-mineral and iron ore clusters in Southern and West Africa. Southern Africa critical mineral clusters could unlock $15-20 billion, and West African bauxite and iron ore clusters could add $17 billion.
market_sizing.source_title: African bedrock: How the continent’s minerals can help power the world

demand_drivers.description: Deployment of generative AI (gen AI) tools to improve safety, environmental awareness, risk mitigation, and compliance monitoring across the mining value chain in Africa.

new_opportunities.description: Gen AI can add significant economic value by optimizing production, predicting maintenance issues, refining drill targeting, and increasing exploration hit rates in African mining operations.

market_sizing.methodology: McKinsey's estimate for the economic value gen AI could add to Africa's mining sector if deployed at scale, with opportunities spanning the entire value chain from safety to compliance.
market_sizing.source_title: African bedrock: How the continent’s minerals can help power the world
